topicTitle: 16.2 Types of Errors in Experimental Measurements
explanation: Random errors are statistical in nature; taking the mean of multiple trials tends to cancel out positive and negative fluctuations, reducing their effect on the final result. Systematic errors cannot be reduced this way.

topicTitle: 16.2 Types of Errors in Experimental Measurements
explanation: Faulty or uncalibrated equipment leads to instrumental systematic errors that shift all readings by a constant amount in the same direction, reducing accuracy without affecting precision.

topicTitle: 16.2 Types of Errors in Experimental Measurements
explanation: Closeness of measurements to each other indicates high precision (low random error). Distance from the true value indicates low accuracy, which is typically caused by a systematic error shifting all values in the same direction.
